info.title: Pidgen Public API: pending project readiness routes
info.description: A Project's readiness, as the App Service states it: the inspection of its repository, the findings (one per area), the questions it could not answer, the proposed setup (`.pidgen/pidgen.toml` and the scripts it names), and the rehearsal that proves it on a worker. GET …/readiness reads it; GET …/readiness/proposal/archive downloads the proposed files as a gzip-compressed tar archive, each entry a path under `.pidgen/` from the repository root with its mode; POST …/readiness/proposal/pull-request opens the pull request that proposes them; POST …/readiness/answers answers questions and inspects again; POST …/readiness/rehearse requests a rehearsal, followed by reading …/readiness until its `rehearsal` settles; POST …/readiness/doctor runs the Project doctor, which answers whether the setup is why work fails. Readiness never gates admission. When the server publishes them, they are pulled with contracts/openapi.json and this file is deleted. Settled here where the stated contract is silent: the schema names, the error codes, and the archive's media type. Every route takes the bearer credential and the X-PIDGEN-Account header like the published routes.

get.description: The Project's readiness: the latest inspection and its findings, the questions, the proposal and the latest rehearsal. An unknown Project, and another Account's, is 404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.

findings.summary: Inspected, one question open, a draft proposed

get.description: The proposed files as a gzip-compressed tar archive: one regular-file entry per file, its path from the repository root under `.pidgen/` and its mode (0755 for a script, 0644 otherwise), with directory entries for `.pidgen/` and `.pidgen/scripts/`. post.description: Ask a worker to build a throwaway workspace from `ref` through the ordinary provisioning path, run provision, activate, the database step and the tests, and tear it down. Answers the rehearsal, `queued`; read …/readiness to follow it. 404 READINESS_PROPOSAL_NOT_FOUND when there is nothing to rehearse; 409 REHEARSAL_IN_PROGRESS while another runs; 409 NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER when no connected worker can run the Project.

post.description: Ask whether the workspace setup is why work in the Project fails. Reads the setup files at the base branch through a worker, the connected workers' preflight and the last `since_days` days (7 by default) of the Project's runs, and answers the report when the checks are done (under a minute). Changes nothing, except that `propose_fix` opens the fix as a pull request when the setup is the problem and the doctor has a template for it. 404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND; 409 FORGE_NOT_CONNECTED when `propose_fix` cannot open the pull request.

bearerAuth.description: A CLI token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Obtain one with the device-code login: POST /api/v1/auth/device, then poll POST /api/v1/auth/device/token.

ReadinessInspection.title: ReadinessInspection
ReadinessInspection.description: The latest inspection of the Project's repository.

state.description: `inspecting` while the files are read, `inspected` once the findings are in, `failed` when the repository could not be read (`failure` says why).

ref.description: The branch read, the Project's base branch.

anyOf.description: The commit read; null until it is known.

source.description: `forge`: read through the forge API with the Project's token; `worker`: a worker read a plain git remote.

anyOf.description: When it finished; null while inspecting.
Why the repository could not be read; null unless `failed`.

ReadinessArea.title: ReadinessArea
ReadinessArea.description: One finding: what the inspection found in one area of the repository.

title.description: The area's name as a person reads it, e.g. `Tools on the worker`.

state.description: `ok`: nothing to do; `proposed`: the proposal covers it; `needs_you`: a person must act (`ask` says how); `cannot_tell`: a question must be answered before Pidgen proposes anything; `pending`: not known yet (inspecting, or a worker must answer).

summary.description: What was found, in one sentence.

anyOf.description: What the proposal does about it; null when nothing.
What a person must do; null unless the area needs someone.

ReadinessQuestion.title: ReadinessQuestion
ReadinessQuestion.description: A question the inspection could not answer from the files. Answering it (POST …/readiness/answers) inspects again with the answer.

question_id.description: The question's id, used to answer it.

question.description: The question, as a person reads it.

evidence.description: What the inspection found that raised it.

choices.description: The answers it takes; empty when any text is an answer.

anyOf.description: The answer used when none is given; null when there is none.
The answer recorded; null while the question is open.

ProposalFile.title: ProposalFile
ProposalFile.description: One proposed file, by its path from the repository root.

path.description: The path from the repository root, under `.pidgen/`.

executable.description: Whether the file is executable (a script the manifest names).

ProposalPullRequest.title: ProposalPullRequest
ProposalPullRequest.description: The pull request that proposes the setup.

url.description: The pull request on the forge.

state.description: Its state as the forge reports it.

ReadinessProposal.title: ReadinessProposal
ReadinessProposal.description: The setup Pidgen proposes from the findings: `.pidgen/pidgen.toml` and the scripts it names.

state.description: `draft`: not written anywhere; `pull_request_open`: proposed as `pull_request`; `merged`: on the base branch.

assumptions.description: What the proposal assumes, one sentence each.

RehearsalStep.title: RehearsalStep
RehearsalStep.description: One step of a rehearsal, as the worker reported it.

step.description: The step: `provision`, `activate`, `database` or `tests`, in the order they run.

anyOf.description: Its exit status; null while running or when skipped.
How long it took; null while running or when skipped.
What it reported, e.g. `212 passed`, or why it failed.

Rehearsal.title: Rehearsal
Rehearsal.description: A rehearsal: a worker builds a throwaway workspace from `ref`, runs the setup and the tests, and tears it down.

state.description: `queued` until a worker takes it, `running`, then `passed`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

ref.description: The branch rehearsed: the proposal's branch, or the base branch once merged.

anyOf.description: The commit rehearsed; null until a worker has fetched it.
The worker that runs it; null while queued.

steps.description: The steps reported so far, in the order they ran.

anyOf.description: The outcome in one sentence: what worked, or the step that failed, why, and the fix; null until it has settled.
When it settled; null until then.
The full log, staged as an artifact; null until it has settled.

Readiness.title: Readiness
Readiness.description: A Project's readiness: the latest inspection, its findings (one per area), the open questions, the proposal and the latest rehearsal. Readiness never gates admission.

anyOf.description: The repository, as the Project names it; null when it has none.

areas.description: One finding per area, in the order the report shows them.

questions.description: The questions, answered ones included (their `answer` set).

updated_at.description: When any of it last changed.

value.description: The answer: one of the question's `choices` when it has any.

anyOf.description: The branch to rehearse; omitted or null: the open proposal's branch, or the base branch once the setup is merged.

DoctorCheck.title: DoctorCheck
DoctorCheck.description: One finding of the Project doctor, in the words the Project page shows.

state.description: `ok`; `needs_you`, worth a person's look but not why work fails; `failed`, a reason work fails.

summary.description: The finding in one line, Tickets named by key.

anyOf.description: What the failure said, verbatim (a hook's stderr, a test's signature); null when there is none.

tickets.description: The Tickets the finding concerns, by key, in the order they failed.

anyOf.description: The change that introduced it, its Ticket by key; null when unknown.
The change to make, as a sentence naming the file; null when nothing is to change.

DoctorGroup.title: DoctorGroup
DoctorGroup.description: One of the doctor's six groups of checks.

group.description: Which group: the setup files on the base branch, the connected workers, the Project's secrets, the workspaces and the tests in the window, and the drift since the last rehearsal.

title.description: The group's heading, e.g. `Setup files on main` or `Workspaces, 7 days`.

checks.description: Its findings, the failing ones first.

DoctorFix.title: DoctorFix
DoctorFix.description: The fix for the setup, when the setup is the problem.

summary.description: The fix in one line; the pull request's title when the doctor has a template for it.

anyOf.description: The template the doctor writes the fix from (`activate_warn`, `executable_bit`, `timeout`); null when it has none and the person makes the change.

retry.description: The Tickets to retry, by key, once the fix is on the base branch.

ProjectDoctorReport.title: ProjectDoctorReport
ProjectDoctorReport.description: The Project doctor's report: whether the workspace setup is why work in the Project fails, the six groups of checks, and the fix.

anyOf.description: The repository as the forge names it, e.g. `acme/storefront`.

ref.description: The base branch whose setup files were read.

anyOf.description: The commit read; null when the setup files could not be read.

since.description: The start of the window of runs read.

verdict.description: `setup`: the setup is the problem (the CLI exits 1); `code`: it is not, and `summary` says what did fail and why it is code; `unclear`: the doctor cannot tell, and `summary` says which failures it could not classify.

summary.description: The verdict as a sentence with its evidence: the failing step, the count, the Tickets by key and the change that introduced it; or what did fail and why it is code.

groups.description: The six groups, in order: setup_files, workers, secrets, workspaces, tests, drift.

failed_tickets.description: Every Ticket that failed in the window, by key.

anyOf.description: Why to rehearse now, e.g. `refresh the timings from main (about 6 min)`; null when the last rehearsal is current.
How many days of runs to read; omitted or null: 7.

propose_fix.description: Open the fix as a pull request when the setup is the problem and the doctor has a template for it; `fix.pull_request` is then that pull request. Default false.

PublicError.description: The body of every error a published route answers with; switch on error.code.
PublicError.title: PublicError

PublicErrorDetail.description: What went wrong: a stable code, a message, and optional context.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code, e.g. PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.
code.title: Code

message.description: Human-readable explanation; not a stable interface.
message.title: Message

details.description: Structured context for the error, when there is any.
details.title: Details

request_id.description: The request's X-Request-ID, for correlating with logs.
request_id.title: Request Id

PublicErrorDetail.title: PublicErrorDetail
